name: Can interior log walls be sealed if they already have an existing finish?

mainEntity.name: Can interior log walls be sealed if they already have an existing finish?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can seal interior log walls without stripping them, provided the existing stain or finish is stable, clean, and not peeling. However, if the old finish is flaky, waxy, or oil-saturated, new sealants will struggle to bond. A practical tradeoff is choosing between spot-cleaning joints versus full wall refinishing: spot-prepping joint lines saves significant labor cost, but any incompatible clear coat applied over dirty wood will lock in discoloration. Having a finish specialist assess your current interior coating ensures the sealant adheres tightly without requiring unnecessary full-wall stripping.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, as long as the underlying finish is sound and clean; degraded or flaking coats must be prepped or removed along the joint line for proper adhesion.
